method: One logical change at a time: hypothesis -> minimal implementation -> focused tests -> same M4 evaluation (scripts/run_m4_evaluation.py, null LLM, offline) -> compare with the frozen baseline -> accept or reject. Rejected variants were reverted before the next experiment.

experiments.name: Assistant job discovery uses the requested area
experiments.hypothesis: Discovery ignores the message: match_jobs_for_resume always retrieves with the resume's own terms.
experiments.change: assistant_intent.extract_discovery_request strips generic discovery wording (no domain lists); when area words remain they drive retrieval via an optional query on match_jobs_for_profile/match_jobs_for_resume, while scoring stays resume-based. Generic requests keep resume-driven discovery.
experiments.regressions: none (all other metrics identical; 74 assistant/matching tests passed)

experiments.name: Conversational routing: self-comparison, learning-priority follow-ups, free-form discovery wording
experiments.hypothesis: 'Compare me with JOB-X' is routed as a two-job comparison; learning-priority follow-ups and 'find <area> jobs' phrasings match no keyword.
experiments.change: Deterministic regex rules in assistant_intent.classify_intent: student-as-object comparison -> JOB_MATCH_EXPLANATION (job<->job comparison unchanged); learn/study/focus verb + priority word -> LEARNING_GUIDANCE (whole-word, so 'machine learning' does not fire); discovery verb + opportunity noun -> JOB_DISCOVERY after all specific rules.
experiments.regressions: none (66 assistant tests; existing intent tests unchanged incl. 'Compare these two roles for me' staying a comparison)

experiments.name: Substantive answers to free-form career questions
experiments.hypothesis: General questions get a fixed capability message.
experiments.change: None implemented. A substantive answer requires the LLM path; the automated evaluation is deterministic/null-LLM, so no improvement could be measured, and changing the fixed text to pass the check would be overfitting.

experiments.name: Shared bidirectional related-skill table with partial credit for required and preferred skills
experiments.hypothesis: Matching is exact-term only, while Skill Gap already has a related-technology table.
experiments.change: RELATED_TERMS moved to skill_relationships.py with related_terms() used in both directions by matching, skill gap and customization; matching gave 0.5 credit for related-only required and preferred skills.
experiments.regressions: B (1/4 required) overtook A (3/4 required), breaking the required>preferred property; one new grounding violation (related note placed in strengths).

experiments.name: E3a + preferred credit scaled by required coverage
experiments.hypothesis: Gating preferred credit restores required-skill importance.
experiments.change: _match_score multiplied preferred score by required score.
experiments.regressions: P001 (60.0 -> 58.5) and P005 (51.2 -> 48.2) fell below their expected minimum scores.

experiments.name: E3b + weights required 0.45 / preferred 0.10
experiments.hypothesis: Raising the required weight widens A-B.
experiments.regressions: A-B only 7.3 (target 10 not met); P005 score behaviour regressed.

experiments.name: Shared related-skill table; related credit for preferred skills only
experiments.hypothesis: A hard requirement needs direct evidence (Skill Gap reports related evidence for it as 'partial, not met'); related technologies are legitimate partial evidence for nice-to-have skills.
experiments.change: skill_relationships.related_terms() (bidirectional, normalised with normalize_term) shared by matching, skill gap and customization; matching gives 0.5 credit only to related preferred skills, keeps them in 'missing', and explains them in the reasoning. Also fixed a latent defect: the table spelled 'node.js' while normalize_term produces 'nodejs', so Node.js relationships never fired.
experiments.regressions: none. Targets A-B >= 10 (4.5) and C-D >= 10 (5.0) NOT met; C > D now holds (was equal).

experiments.name: One education assessment shared by matching and skill gap
experiments.hypothesis: The services use divergent keyword logic; matching has no partial tier and neither recognises 'computing'/'engineering' as requirement fields.
experiments.change: education_assessment.assess_education_text (met / partial / not_met / unknown, whole-word field detection; 'relevant X program' names fields, 'related field' accepts related technical fields; a bare B.Sc or 'it' is not a field) consumed by both services.
experiments.regressions: none (M2 profile outcomes identical; 145 focused tests)

experiments.name: Naming the target opportunity is not a skill claim
experiments.hypothesis: The validator removed a cover-letter opening because the job title 'FastAPI Intern' contains a skill the student lacks.
experiments.change: check_fabrication/validate_summary/validate_cover_letter accept allowed_phrases; customization passes the job title and company so exact occurrences are masked for the unsupported-keyword check only (metric/leadership/years checks still see the full text). Applied to the final validator and, after the prompt review, to the LLM-layer pre-validation (the prompt requires the letter to open with the job title and company). The M4 evaluator applies the same rule; a 10th fault injection (role named AND skill claimed in one sentence) proves claims are still caught.

experiments.name: Retrieval confidence for off-topic queries
experiments.hypothesis: Score overlap makes a similarity threshold unsafe; whether the query's vocabulary exists in the catalogue separates off-topic from genuine queries.

C_query_term_coverage.<0.5: 11/12 flagged, 0 genuine flagged (miss: RO01 UI UX design)

variants.held_out_check_of_C: off-topic 10/10 flagged; genuine 1/10 flagged ('Linux system administration trainee', coverage 0.33)

experiments.change: retrieval_confidence.query_confidence (coverage of query content words in a catalogue vocabulary derived at runtime from titles, domains and skills; no hard-coded domains) -> each search result carries query_confidence ('confident' | 'unsupported_area'). Results are never suppressed. Careers page shows a notice; assistant discovery says the area is not covered.

result.false_negative: RO01 'UI UX design internship with Figma'

experiments.decision: ACCEPT (variant C as a flag; A, B, E rejected)

experiments.name: Provenance of profile-only (self-reported) skills
experiments.hypothesis: Matching, skill gap and customization present profile-only skills as demonstrated.
experiments.change: Skill gap (and customization, which reuses its reasons) says the skill is self-reported with no resume evidence and uses confidence 0.70 instead of 0.95; matching records self_reported_skills and names them in the reasoning. Skills still count — the student supplied them. Evaluator review check now flags only an unqualified 'demonstrated' presentation.

experiments.name: Extra title/type chunk per posting
experiments.change: 4th chunk (1280 vectors), built in memory only.
experiments.regressions: precision@5 and recall@5 below baseline (0.6538 / 0.8735); index +33%.

experiments.name: Title/type prefix on every chunk
experiments.change: All three chunks prefixed; canonical index rebuilt (v1.1) after the M4 evaluation looked clean.
experiments.regressions: tests/test_job_matching_integration.py: the ML-student profile's best Machine Learning posting fell from rank 2 to rank 5, so no ML job appeared in the top 5. Missed by the first acceptance check (M4 ML profile P001 accepts Data Science as primary).

experiments.name: Title/type prefix on the overview chunk only
experiments.hypothesis: Title and opportunity type are what distinguish postings inside a domain; adding them only where the overview describes the role avoids diluting skill chunks.
experiments.change: job_chunking: overview chunk leads with '<title> (<employment type>). '; INDEX_VERSION 1.2; canonical index rebuilt with scripts/build_job_vector_index.py (960 vectors). Original v1.0 index backed up outside the repo during the experiment.

experiments.name: Local-first embedding model loading
experiments.hypothesis: SentenceTransformer(name) performs Hugging Face hub checks on every cold start (hung the test suite >20 min when the hub was unreachable).
experiments.change: embedding_service.get_embedding_model loads with local_files_only=True first; downloads only on a cache miss and only if EMBEDDING_ALLOW_DOWNLOAD (default true); otherwise raises a clear EmbeddingError.

experiments.name: In-process caches for the immutable dataset and vector store
experiments.hypothesis: Each request re-reads and re-validates the 320-record dataset (twice per matching request) and re-reads the FAISS index.
experiments.change: load_job_postings and load_vector_store cache their validated result keyed by file path, mtime and size (plus model name for the index); every validation still runs when a file changes; callers get fresh lists; clear_* functions reset them. No user data is cached.
experiments.regressions: none (cache invalidation and validation-after-change covered by tests)

experiments.name: Token usage capture
experiments.change: OpenAICompatibleProvider records the provider's reported `usage` (prompt/completion/total tokens) in last_usage and logs it; nothing is estimated.
experiments.result: Verified with fake HTTP responses only. Token usage not measured in automated baseline because live LLM execution is intentionally disabled.

experiments.name: Prompt review
experiments.result: All four system prompts (customization, interview prep, assistant, mock answer) already define role, inputs, an evidence list with ids, task, constraints, a strict JSON output and grounding rules. No prompt text was changed: improvements could not be measured without live LLM calls. One testable prompt/validator conflict was fixed under E5 (the prompt requires naming the job title; the LLM-layer validator rejected titles containing unsupported skills).

remaining.test_general_career_question_gets_a_subs: Needs the LLM path; not measurable with the deterministic evaluation (E2b).
